messages.text: Donald ends retirement to make dramatic Rams return

metadata.summary: Aaron Donald has officially come out of retirement and will return for the Los Angeles Rams this season.
metadata.content: Aaron Donald: Los Angeles Rams legendary defensive tackle comes out of retirement for 2026 season | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to content Aaron Donald: Los Angeles Rams legendary defensive tackle comes out of retirement for 2026 season Aaron Donald has agreed a one-year deal with the Rams after two and a half years in retirement; the 35-year-old joins a defensive line where he and Myles Garrett hold five of the last nine Defensive Player of the Year awards between them Sunday 30 August 2026 21:53, UK Image: Aaron Donald celebrates the Los Angeles Rams' Super Bowl win in the 2021 season Aaron Donald has officially come out of retirement and will return for the Los Angeles Rams this season. The 35-year-old is coming back after two and a half years away from the game to form a defensive pairing with Myles Garrett that will alarm every offensive line in the NFL. The Rams confirmed Donald's decision on Sunday at the end of weeks of talks and almost two months of workouts at the club's facility, where Donald tested whether his body could stand another season. He has signed a one-year contract, with ESPN reporting the deal is worth at least $20m and built heavily on incentives. Ben Duckett - 4 Batting: 17 and 1 A forgettable Test which saw the England opener face only 26 deliveries across his two innings. He was one of a number of batters who perhaps felt a touch unfortunate to be given out lbw in the first innings to deliveries that, at first glance, looked to be going over the stumps, only to be shown otherwise after a timely Pakistan review. His second-innings failure, however, simply owed to a poor shot as he chipped one straight to mid-off.
